chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever collects an ostrich egg while he is in the state of ihram, upon him is to send a male camel in the number equal to the count of the eggs from the camels, for perhaps all of them spoil, and perhaps all of them hatch, and perhaps some of them are viable and some spoil; whatever the camels give birth to, they are a offering (hady) reaching the Ka'bah.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of holy consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.هَدْي: Sacrificial offering brought to the Ka'bah

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for an ostrich egg collected by a pilgrim in ihram?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Istibsar highlights the Shia juristic approach to 'gharama' (compensation) in cases of uncertainty regarding the viability of the ostrich egg, distinguishing it from standard animal sacrifices. By mandating the release of a male camel for each egg, the Imam addresses the variable outcome—whether the egg hatches or spoils—ensuring the pilgrim fulfills their obligation proportionally to the potential loss. This reflects the broader principle in Shia fiqh of balancing strict adherence to ritual purity with practical equity in financial compensation.
